brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full plus piece:0,1,0;half-n, joined by jointBolt:0#0,0#5, with end caps on the open faces.

bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-half-div3 is one bin with 3 compartments that drops into the cell and hangs on its rim, so it lifts out. Screws, nuts and standoffs are staged in it. You asked for bins and this is a single bin. It sits under the handle lid, so the props in it can't be seen in the view.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base and is shown open. It is very tight inside: no screw, nut, solder-reel or tweezers props fit in it.

handle:0,0,0;top sits on the top cover of the bin cell. That cover also works as a lid that keeps the small parts in when you carry it. The configurator checks fit only, not how much weight the handle can take.
The build is compact (two cells) and has a top handle. The configurator can't check weight or strength when it's carried loaded.

finish.summary: I built a two-cell organizer with 28 parts. It has a full hex base holding a removable 3-compartment small-parts bin. A lid with a carry handle closes that cell. Beside it is a north-half base with a drawer under its own cover. I added end caps on the open faces and a joint bolt so the cells can't slide apart. The final check found no rule errors and no mesh collisions.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
